_comment: Created 2026-10-02 during Activia USA onboarding. NOT yet run for real — pipeline deliberately not started until all source exports validate clean (per explicit user instruction). Brand colors, competitors[], sem_qv.competitor_blocklist, and ga4_ads_file_id are all still TBD/missing real values; qs_sheet_id (Quality Report) and both Conversions exports are entirely unregistered in the source registry as of this writing. See brands/activia-usa's _masterlist_comment, _keyword_study_comment, and _se_ranking_comment below for the specific data-quality issues found and how the pipeline was adjusted to handle them.
_brand_colors_comment: Sampled 2026-10-02 directly from activia.us.com's live production CSS (curl + grep for hex codes, then confirmed via the site's own literal named CSS custom properties: --activia-green, --activia-green-light, --activia-yellow) — not a screenshot guess. --activia-green was by far the dominant dark color across the homepage (56+ occurrences incl. near-identical shade variants #045025/#04551D), --activia-yellow the dominant light background (97 occurrences) despite reading as cream, not literal yellow, to the eye.
_gsc_comment: gsc_p1_prefix/gsc_p2_prefix deliberately left UNSET. The real GSC export (Queries tab) auto-detects correctly via _detect_gsc_prefixes() — confirmed against real data: it finds '4/1/26 - 6/30/26' as P1 and '1/1/26 - 3/31/26' as P2 exactly matching this brand's real period. Hardcoding these instead risks a documented silent-failure mode: if the hardcoded text doesn't exactly match the sheet's real column names, norm_gsc() doesn't raise an exception — every row's lookup returns 0 for both periods, gets dropped by the c1==0 and c2==0 filter, and the function returns an empty list with NO error, only an easy-to-miss 'GSC: 0/XXXX kept' log line. Leaving these unset routes through the auto-detect path instead, which was verified to work correctly for this brand's real export.
_se_ranking_comment: se_exclude_url_prefixes added 2026-10-02 after finding the real SE Ranking export is a whole-domain history report, not US-scoped: verified 4,252 of 4,524 rows (94%) are real US-search keywords with legitimate position/volume/CPC data, but Google currently ranks a non-US locale page for them (genuine cross-market SEO issue, not an export mistake). pipeline/ingest.py's norm_se() was extended to blank just se_url_path for these rows (not drop them) when exclude_url_prefixes is set, so the keyword's real SE Ranking data stays usable everywhere (SE matching, Position/Volume on the Masterlist) while GA4 conversion pro-rata distribution (which matches by URL) won't misattribute a conversion to the wrong market's page. Verified against real data before settling on this design — an earlier attempt that dropped the whole row would have discarded 94% of the export's keyword data.
_keyword_study_comment: Per explicit user instruction ('these are all we have, make sure the pipeline is adjusted to accept it as is') — no new KS data is coming, the pipeline is adjusted around what exists. Real sheet ('Nov 2025 - Activia US - Keyword Study', tab 'Keyword Study - US', 19,872 rows) is a frozen Nov 2025 snapshot: TOPICS/CATEGORY/SUB-CATEGORY carry real per-row values (confirmed, e.g. 'smoothies near me' -> RECIPE/RECIPE/smoothie) and norm_ks() already handles its TOPIC/TOPICS naming variance, but it has (a) no LANG column — rows fall back to this config's top-level lang='EN', harmless since 100% of real sampled rows were English with no French/CA-market contamination found; (b) monthly search-volume history that stops at Oct 2025, with zero data for the real Apr-Jun 2026 period — Average Search Volume would be blank for every single row from KS alone; (c) none of the Oikos-style 13 taxonomy tag columns (Questions, Taste, Ingredient, etc.) exist here at all — only a 'Brand' (singular) column does. Mitigations: taxonomy_tags below is trimmed to just ['Brands'] so norm_ks()'s built-in Brand/Brands singular-plural aliasing (ingest.py:235) picks up the one real tag column that exists, instead of requesting 12 columns that will never be there; enrich_taxonomy is enabled below so Claude backfills Average Search Volume indirectly is NOT covered by this (that's a volume problem, not a classification problem) but DOES fill in TOPICS/CATEGORY/SUB-CATEGORY for whatever Masterlist rows don't match into this KS sheet at all, same gap class found and fixed for International Delight. Real fix for Average Search Volume is enrich_volumes()/enrich_monthly_volumes() hitting the live SE Ranking API post-write (pipeline/enrich.py) — independent of this stale KS sheet, requires SE_RANKING_API_KEY in .env (already set, shared across brands) and se_months_p1/p2 above pointing at the real Apr-Jun/Jan-Mar 2026 months, which the Masterlist header_corrections below also need to expose as real columns. NOT yet checked: the same file's unwired 'Volumes US' tab (62 cols, 27,025 rows) might be a fresher volume source — worth checking before fully accepting the Nov 2025 snapshot as final, but out of scope for 'accept it as-is'.

taxonomy_prompt.brand_context: Activia, a probiotic yogurt brand (gut health, digestion, probiotics)

_topic_order_comment: Added 2026-10-03 per pre-dashboard-build audit finding: build_html.py reads 'topic_order' (not 'territories') for the Overview tab's Coverage-by-Topics gauges — 'territories' only controls the Core Search Territories glossary/deep-dive panel. Left unset, the Overview tab would silently auto-sort by volume instead of this curated order. Mirrors territories' key order above.
_territories_comment:
Added 2026-10-03, before the first real pipeline run, per explicit user request to lock down taxonomy/territory ahead of the masterlist build. build_html.py's _patch_module() reads this 'territories' dict directly into TERRITORY_DEFINITIONS/TERRITORY_TOPICS with NO fallback (list(cfg.get('territories', {}).keys())) — leaving it unset would silently render an empty Core Search Territories panel and glossary once the dashboard is built, same class of silent-blank-on-missing-config bug already found and documented elsewhere in this file. Key order here IS the dashboard display order. Descriptions/examples grounded in shared/brand-guidelines/activia.md (Danone's real Activia brand brief) AND a real crawl of activia.us.com done 2026-10-03 (sitemap.xml + homepage nav) — real site sections confirmed: Probiotic Products (Cups/Dailies/Drinks; Probiotics/Fiber/Zero Added Sugar/ProActive lines), Gut Health/Wellness/Probiotics education articles, the Gut Health Challenge (14-day habit program — matches CONSUMER HABITS), Healthcare Professionals/clinical-strain content, and corporate/navigational pages (About, Press, FAQ, Where to Buy) — no recipe section anywhere. Topics list mirrors Silk's set (BRAND/PRODUCT/COMPETITOR/GENERIC/HEALTH/RECIPE/CONSUMER HABITS/OTHER) rather than Oikos's (which adds a protein-specific SOURCE OF PROTEIN territory that doesn't apply to a gut-health yogurt brand). HEALTH is Activia's single most central territory (the entire brand promise is 'Supports gut health*') — judgment call to treat it as a priority territory alongside BRAND rather than a generic-tier one, worth revisiting once real classified volume shows how big it actually is. No numeric coverage_target per territory — confirmed build_html.py/build_html_oikos.py only read a flat coverage_targets.brand/generic/competitor split (inherited from brands/defaults.json: 10/3/2), not a per-territory target field, so one wasn't added here to avoid dead config.

RECIPE special case: counted the real frozen Keyword Study sheet's TOPICS column directly (19,871 rows) before finalizing this — RECIPE is actually the SINGLE LARGEST topic at 10,248 rows (51.6%), ahead of HEALTH (6,439) and PRODUCTS (3,162), and sampling confirms these are legitimate food/recipe search terms (smoothies, overnight oats, chia pudding, spinach-artichoke dip), not mislabeled noise. User flagged that Activia's real content plan has no recipe pillar (confirmed true by the site crawl) and asked whether RECIPE still belongs in the taxonomy. Explicit user decision: keep RECIPE as a tracked territory — not because it's a content priority, but because it's useful competitive intelligence (shows leadership what yogurt-recipe-focused competitors are capturing that Activia, by deliberate gut-health-first positioning, is not). Kept the exact key 'RECIPE' (not renamed) so it keeps matching the real KS sheet's existing classified value and match_ks.py's pre-existing matches stay intact; only desc/intent/examples were rewritten to frame it explicitly as a competitive-gap signal, not a content-plan recommendation. taxonomy_prompt.topics also keeps RECIPE so future unmatched/new keywords with genuine recipe intent keep classifying correctly going forward instead of being forced into an ill-fitting bucket.

BRAND.desc: Keywords that explicitly name Activia, its core product lines (Probiotic Yogurt cups, Probiotic Dailies drinkable yogurt, ProActive, Zero Added Sugar, Fiber), or brand variants and misspellings. The highest-intent territory — users already know the brand.

PRODUCT.desc: Generic product-type keywords — probiotic yogurt, drinkable yogurt, high-fiber yogurt — where Activia is a natural answer but the brand isn't named. Captures shoppers comparing yogurt types or probiotic formats.

COMPETITOR.desc: Keywords naming competing yogurt and probiotic-drink brands (Chobani, Yoplait, Yakult, Stonyfield, Lifeway Kefir). Activia can capture switcher traffic and conquest clicks via SEM on these terms.

GENERIC.desc: Broad, non-branded category queries about probiotic foods and gut-supportive nutrition with no specific brand intent. High volume, top-of-funnel entry point for shoppers new to the category.

HEALTH.desc: Gut health, digestion, and microbiome queries — Activia's core brand promise ('Supports gut health*'). Covers the gut-brain connection, digestive wellness, and immunity angles the brand is built to answer.

RECIPE.desc: Recipe and food-use queries (smoothies, overnight oats, dips, puddings) where yogurt is a natural ingredient. Activia's own site has no recipe content — its content strategy centers on gut-health science and digestion rather than general yogurt recipes — but this is real, substantial search volume (51.6% of this brand's full Keyword Study, the single largest topic) that yogurt-recipe-focused competitors actively capture. Tracked as a competitive-intelligence / content-gap territory to show leadership what competitors are doing here, not as a near-term content priority for Activia itself.

CONSUMER HABITS.desc: Occasion and routine queries — breakfast, snacking, New Year resets, seasonal gut-health challenges — that frame probiotic yogurt as part of a daily wellness routine rather than a one-off purchase.

OTHER.desc: Miscellaneous queries including brand misspellings, customer service, coupons, and where-to-buy. Low strategic priority but useful for brand monitoring and defensive coverage.

_masterlist_comment: Real Masterlist ('MASTERLIST - Activia OneSearch', tab 'Listing') was copy-pasted from an Oikos-era template and originally had Oikos's period labels baked into its header row ('Volume Q1 2026'/'Volume Q4 2025' etc.) even though every real source export here is genuinely Q2 2026 vs Q1 2026 data. header_corrections below was the one-time migration that fixed this — RETIRED (emptied) on 2026-10-03 after confirming the live sheet's header row is now fully, correctly labeled (verified cell-by-cell via mcp__google-sheets__readSpreadsheet: every pair reads '... Q2 2026' / '... Q1 2026' with no stale 'Q4 2025' and no duplicates). Do NOT repopulate this dict with the old rename pairs — doing so caused a real, reproducible data-corruption incident: the dict had two chained rules per metric (e.g. 'X Q1 2026'->'X Q2 2026' AND 'X Q4 2025'->'X Q1 2026'); applying it ONCE against the original stale template was correct, but applying it a SECOND time (e.g. on a second pipeline run after the first already fixed the headers) matched the already-correct 'X Q1 2026' P2 column against the FIRST rule and renamed it to 'X Q2 2026' too — leaving two columns both named '...Q2 2026' and zero named '...Q1 2026' for 14 metric pairs (Volume, Coverage, Clics/Impressions OneSearch, Clics/Impr./CTR/Conversions SEO+SEM, Spent SEM, Cost SEO), which crashed run_pipeline.py's ARRAYFORMULA step looking for the now-missing 'Clics OneSearch Q1 2026' column. Manually repaired via a targeted batchWrite (renamed the 14 duplicate second-occurrence cells back to their correct 'Q1 2026' labels by column position) before retiring this dict. If a brand's Masterlist header ever needs a similar one-time fix again, apply it, confirm the sheet is correct, then immediately empty header_corrections the same way — never leave chained Q1->Q2 / Q4->Q1 style rename pairs active across multiple runs.
_ga4_ads_comment: Fixed 2026-10-02 — the real re-pulled export (replacing the earlier one that was missing the keyword dimension) now has 'Session Google Ads query' alongside 'Landing page + query string', in GA4 Compare mode. Verified directly against pipeline/sem_qv.py's real read_ga4_ads_compare() + calculate_qv_sem() before registering: columns resolve with zero collisions (keyword: 'Session Google Ads query', landing_page: 'Landing page + query string'), and QV SEM totals (14,278 for Q1 2026, 4,465 for Q2 2026) match the sheet's own Grand Total 'Key events' row exactly, 0 unassigned. ga4_ads_file_id_p2 stays TBD/unused — this one file covers both periods via Compare mode, auto-detected by detect_ga4_compare_mode(), same as Silk/ID's real exports.
_competitors_comment: Drafted 2026-10-02 from the real Keyword Study sheet's own competitor-tracking columns (5x 'Pos. Google <competitor>.com' rank-tracking columns) rather than waiting on a fresh raw candidate list like Oikos/Silk/ID each got from the registry — confirmed real brand mentions in the KS sheet's own 'Brand' column for 4 of these 5 (Chobani, Yoplait, Yakult, Stonyfield all appear repeatedly; Lifeway Kefir didn't appear in the ~3,000-row sample checked but is still a real tracked competitor per the position columns). This is a starting list grounded in what the brand's own SEO team already tracks, not an exhaustive market scan — likely incomplete (e.g. no Fage, Siggi's, Dannon, Two Good mentioned anywhere sampled) and worth a second human pass, same caveat given to Oikos/Silk/ID's lists.
_sem_qv_comment: competitor_blocklist left unset for now — same reasoning as Oikos/Silk/ID: sem_qv.py's tag_sem_recommendations() only matters once TOPICS=='BRAND' rows actually exist, and this brand's pipeline hasn't been run yet. Revisit once a real run produces BRAND-tagged rows, using these same curated patterns as the starting point.
